chain.title: The card behind each operation
chain.desc: Craft Blank Modules for the router's operations. Each specialized module performs a different job; choose the first pair around a simple transfer you can test.

chain.title: One buffer, a sequence of operations
chain.desc: Place a Modular Router and inspect its buffer and module slots. Modules run in their configured order, so plan how items enter the buffer and where they go next.

chain.title: Pull from a neighboring inventory
chain.desc: Configure the Puller Module's direction toward a neighboring inventory and install it. Filter the accepted items and leave enough buffer space for the transfer.

chain.title: Send the buffered item onward
chain.desc: Configure a Sender Module for its intended target and install it after the pull operation. Test a small transfer before feeding the router a mixed inventory.

chain.title: Prepare router-wide upgrades
chain.desc: Craft Blank Upgrades for changes such as speed, stack transfer, or energy storage. These affect the router, while module augments affect one operation.

chain.title: Increase the operation rate
chain.desc: Add Speed Upgrades after the basic route works. Watch the receiving inventory and module order so faster operation does not simply create a buffer jam.

chain.title: Move larger batches
chain.desc: Use Stack Upgrades to raise the amount transferred by supported item operations. Choose a batch size that fits the receiving machine's ingredient needs.

chain.title: Tune one module at a time
chain.desc: Craft Augment Cores and choose an augment supported by the target module. Read its limits instead of assuming every augment can be installed in every operation.

chain.title: Filter a larger item set
chain.desc: Configure a Bulk Item Filter for a module that needs more filter entries. Test the allow or deny behavior before connecting it to valuable storage.

chain.title: Expose the buffer's state
chain.desc: Configure a Detector Module to emit the desired redstone response. Use it to signal a filled buffer or a matching item, then test both active and inactive states.

chain.title: Break a selected block
chain.desc: Configure the Breaker Module's direction and supported tool behavior. Test it in a small controlled space and provide a way to remove the collected item from the buffer.

chain.title: Place a block from the buffer
chain.desc: Configure a Placer Module and supply the desired placeable item. Pair it with deliberate redstone control or filtering so it cannot consume unrelated building materials.

chain.title: Perform a controlled interaction
chain.desc: Configure an Activator Module for the intended click, direction, and held item. Check permissions and any configured energy cost, then test one interaction before automating a farm.

chain.title: Collect nearby dropped items
chain.desc: Set the Vacuum Module's range and filter. Route collected items out of the buffer so a single unwanted drop cannot block the collection system.

chain.title: Release an item into the world
chain.desc: Use a Dropper Module when the next process needs an item entity instead of inventory insertion. Control the destination area and pickup behavior.

chain.title: Aim a longer item throw
chain.desc: Configure the Flinger Module's direction and force, then test with expendable items. Provide a reliable receiving area before sending valuable resources across the room.

chain.title: A retractable virtual structure
chain.desc: Configure the Mk2 Extruder's template for a door, bridge, or similar structure. Its virtual blocks are temporary and drop no normal building material, so it is not a source of free blocks.

chain.title: A separate fluid-transfer route
chain.desc: Configure the Fluid Module and the supported fluid container in the router's buffer. Match source, destination, and transfer direction before joining a production line.

chain.title: Increase fluid transfer throughput
chain.desc: Add Fluid Transfer Upgrades to improve supported fluid-module throughput. These upgrades increase transfer rate; they do not create an internal fluid tank.

chain.title: Send energy to a neighboring machine
chain.desc: Configure the output direction and supply energy through a supported charged buffer item or the router's upgraded internal energy buffer. The module transfers energy rather than generating it.

chain.title: Add an internal energy buffer
chain.desc: Install an Energy Upgrade to give the router internal energy storage. Connect an actual energy source, then use compatible modules to distribute the stored energy.

chain.title: Select a target beyond the first route
chain.desc: Bind a Mk2 Sender to the intended inventory within its supported range. It removes the Mk1 line-of-sight limitation, but the target and inventory side still need correct configuration.

chain.title: Pull from a selected remote inventory
chain.desc: Bind the Mk2 Puller and configure its side and filter. Test the requested items before connecting it to a large shared storage inventory.

chain.title: A route across any distance
chain.desc: Bind the Mk3 Sender to the intended inventory, including another dimension if required. The destination must remain loaded; Modular Routers does not automatically load it for this module.

chain.title: Share a supply between targets
chain.desc: Configure the Distributor's target list and distribution behavior. Test how it handles a full inventory before using it to feed parallel machines.

chain.title: A deliberate player-inventory route
chain.desc: Configure the target player, inventory section, direction, and filters. Start with a harmless test item so automated restocking or deposit only moves the items you intended.

notes: Re-reviewed 2026-10-07 against local Minecraft 1.20.1 JAR item assets and selected recipes/manuals, with official project sources listed separately. Every authored row now has explicit prerequisites; empty lists identify intentional branch roots. The coverage section states the verified versions and remaining limits. This replaces older list-order and item-count claims.

coverage.scope: Authored branched progression; item and component acquisition objectives, not automatic proof that a factory works.
milestones: Parallel item, world, fluid, and energy operations
limits: Some packs change module energy costs and fake-player permissions.
Mk2 extruder blocks are virtual; the Fluid Upgrade changes transfer rate rather than adding a tank.
Pack scripts, recipe changes, and other Minecraft versions require the installed-pack scan; this guide is not a complete mod manual.
coverage.verification: Local JAR item models and English registry names; selected recipes and bundled manuals checked. Not a new in-game playthrough.
